symbols.name: bus
symbols.summary: Put N cables in parallel. `bus` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: N
params.description: is an integer known at compile time that indicates the number of parallel cables

symbols.name: block
symbols.summary: Block - terminate N signals. `block` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: N
params.description: the number of signals to be blocked known at compile time

symbols.name: interpolate
symbols.summary: Linear interpolation between two signals.

params.name: i
params.description: interpolation control between 0 and 1 (0: first input; 1: second input)

symbols.name: repeat
symbols.summary: Repeat an effect N time(s) and take the parallel sum of all intermediate buses.

params.name: N
params.description: Number of repetitions, minimum of 1, a constant numerical expression

params.name: FX
params.description: an arbitrary effect (N inputs and N outputs) that will be repeated

symbols.name: smoo
symbols.summary: Smoothing function based on `smooth` ideal to smooth UI signals (sliders, etc.) down. Approximately, this is a 7 Hz one-pole low-pass considering the coefficient calculation: exp(-2pi*CF/SR). `smoo` is a standard Faust function.
symbols.testCode:
si = library("signals.lib");
smoo_test = hslider("smoo:input", 0, -1, 1, 0.01) : si.smoo;

symbols.name: polySmooth
symbols.summary: A smoothing function based on `smooth` that doesn't smooth when a trigger signal is given. This is very useful when making polyphonic synthesizer to make sure that the value of the parameter is the right one when the note is started.

params.name: g
params.description: the gate/trigger signal used when making polyphonic synths

params.name: s
params.description: the smoothness (see `smooth`)

params.name: d
params.description: the number of samples to wait before the signal start being smoothed after `g` switched to 1

symbols.name: smoothAndH
symbols.summary: A smoothing function based on `smooth` that holds its output signal when a trigger is sent to it. This feature is convenient when implementing polyphonic instruments to prevent some smoothed parameter to change when a note-off event is sent.

params.name: g
params.description: the hold signal (0 for hold, 1 for bypass)

params.name: s
params.description: the smoothness (see `smooth`)

symbols.name: bsmooth
symbols.summary: Block smooth linear interpolation during a block of samples (given by the `ma.BS` value).
symbols.testCode:
si = library("signals.lib");
bsmooth_test = hslider("bsmooth:input", 0, -1, 1, 0.01) : si.bsmooth;

symbols.name: dot
symbols.summary: Dot product for two vectors of size N.

params.name: N
params.description: size of the vectors (int, must be known at compile time)

symbols.name: smooth
symbols.summary: Exponential smoothing by a unity-dc-gain one-pole lowpass. `smooth` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: tau
params.description: desired smoothing time constant in seconds, or

params.name: s
params.description: smoothness between 0 and 1. s=0 for no smoothing, s=0.999 is "very smooth", s>1 is unstable, and s=1 yields the zero signal for all inputs. The exponential time-constant is approximately 1/(1-s) samples, when s is close to (but less than) 1.

symbols.testCode:
si = library("signals.lib");
smooth_test = hslider("smooth:input", 0, -1, 1, 0.01) : si.smooth(0.9);

symbols.name: smoothq
symbols.summary: Smoothing with continuously variable curves from Exponential to Linear, with a constant time.

params.name: time
params.description: seconds to reach target

params.name: q
params.description: curve shape (between 0..1, 0 is Exponential, 1 is Linear)

symbols.testCode:
si = library("signals.lib");
smoothq_test = hslider("smoothq:input", 0, -1, 1, 0.01) : si.smoothq(0.25, 0.5);

symbols.name: cbus
symbols.summary: N parallel cables for complex signals. `cbus` is a standard Faust function.

params.name: N
params.description: is an integer known at compile time that indicates the number of parallel cables.

symbols.name: cmul
symbols.summary: Multiply two complex signals pointwise. `cmul` is a standard Faust function.
notes: - `(r1,i1)` = real and imaginary parts of signal 1 - `(r2,i2)` = real and imaginary parts of signal 2

symbols.name: cconj
symbols.summary: Complex conjugation of a (complex) signal. `cconj` is a standard Faust function.
notes: - `(r1,i1)` = real and imaginary parts of the input signal - `(r1,-i1)` = real and imaginary parts of the output signal

symbols.name: onePoleSwitching
symbols.summary: One pole filter with independent attack and release times.

params.name: att
params.description: the attack tau time constant in second

params.name: rel
params.description: the release tau time constant in second

symbols.name: rev
symbols.summary: Reverse the input signal by blocks of n>0 samples. `rev(1)` is the indentity function. `rev(n)` has a latency of `n-1` samples.

params.name: n
params.description: the block size in samples

symbols.name: vecOp
symbols.summary: This function is a generalisation of Faust's iterators such as `prod` and `sum`, and it allows to perform operations on an arbitrary number of vectors, provided that they all have the same length. Unlike Faust's iterators `prod` and `sum` where the vector size is equal to one and the vector space dimension must be specified by the user, this function will infer the vector space dimension and vector size based on the vectors list that we provide. The outputs of the function are equal to the vector size, whereas the number of inputs is dependent on whether the elements of the vectors provided expect an incoming signal themselves or not. We will see a clarifying example later; in general, the number of total inputs will be the sum of the inputs in each input vector. Note that we must provide a list of at least two vectors, each with a size that is greater or equal to one.

params.name: vectorsList
params.description: is a list of vectors

params.name: op
params.description: is a two-input, one-output operator

symbols.name: bpar
symbols.summary: Balanced `par` where the repeated expression doesn't depend on a variable. The built-in `par` is implemented as an unbalanced tree, and also has to substitute the variable into the repeated expression, which is expensive even when the variable doesn't appear. This version is implemented as a balanced tree (which allows node reuse during tree traversal) and also doesn't search for the variable. This can be much faster than `par` to compile.
symbols.usage: si.bus(N * inputs(f)) : bpar(N, f) : si.bus(N * outputs(f))

params.name: N
params.description: number of repetitions, minimum 1, a constant numerical expression

params.name: f
params.description: an arbitrary expression

io.raw: si.bus(N * inputs(f)) : bpar(N, f) : si.bus(N * outputs(f))

symbols.testCode:
// square each of 4000 inputs
process = si.bpar(4000, (_ <: _, _ : *));

symbols.name: bsum
symbols.summary: Balanced `sum`, see `si.bpar`.

params.name: N
params.description: number of repetitions, minimum 1, a constant numerical expression

params.name: f
params.description: an arbitrary expression with 1 output.

symbols.testCode:
// square each of 1000 inputs and add the results
process = si.bsum(1000, (_ <: _, _ : *));

symbols.name: bprod
symbols.summary: Balanced `prod`, see `si.bpar`.

params.name: N
params.description: number of repetitions, minimum 1, a constant numerical expression

params.name: f
params.description: an arbitrary expression with 1 output.

symbols.testCode:
// Add 8000 consecutive inputs (in pairs) and multiply the results
process = si.bprod(4000, +);
